changes.before: Drugs that kill fast-dividing cells. Still cures several cancers, and is also the 'warhead' inside newer smart drugs.
changes.after: These medicines can kill cancer cells or stop their growth. Their benefits and harms depend on the drug, treatment plan and cancer setting.
changes.disposition: Corrected simplified English from the adopted source-backed definition; no new language review.

changes.before: Chemotherapy drugs like cisplatin and carboplatin that tangle up DNA. Central to treating lung, ovarian, bladder, and triple-negative breast cancer.
changes.after: Platinum medicines can attach to DNA and link sites together. That does not by itself show that a cell dies or that a treatment will work.
changes.disposition: Corrected simplified English from the adopted source-backed definition; no new language review.

changes.before: Drugs that jam the enzyme that untangles DNA when cells copy themselves. Weak on their own, but powerful when delivered by an antibody-drug.
changes.after: These medicines can trap an enzyme on DNA during a temporary cut. Further damage depends on the medicine, exposure and cell response.
changes.disposition: Corrected simplified English from the adopted source-backed definition; no new language review.

changes.before: Capecitabine (Xeloda), from Roche, is a tablet form of the chemotherapy fluorouracil that is a backbone of bowel cancer treatment and a standard option in advanced breast cancer.
changes.after: The body converts capecitabine tablets into fluorouracil. Taking a medicine by mouth does not remove the risk of serious harm.
changes.disposition: Corrected simplified English from the adopted source-backed definition; no new language review.

changes.before: Chemotherapy means drugs that kill rapidly dividing cells by damaging their DNA or division machinery, hitting cancer hardest but also hair, gut lining and bone marrow.
changes.after: Chemotherapy medicines affect different cell processes. They can kill cancer cells or slow their growth, and healthy cells can be affected too.
changes.disposition: Corrected simplified English from the adopted source-backed definition; no new language review.

changes.before: A regimen is a named recipe of drugs, doses and timing, and a cycle is one round of it, usually two to four weeks, giving normal tissues time to recover.
changes.after: A regimen sets out the medicines, amounts and timing. A cycle is a defined period of treatment and recovery; its length depends on the plan.
changes.disposition: Corrected simplified English from the adopted source-backed definition; no new language review.

changes.before: Anthracyclines are a family of red chemotherapy drugs that damage cancer DNA, cornerstones of breast cancer, lymphoma and leukaemia treatment, but they weaken the heart with cumulative doses.
changes.after: Anthracyclines affect DNA and an enzyme that cuts and reseals it. They can also harm the heart, sometimes after treatment has ended.
changes.disposition: Corrected simplified English from the adopted source-backed definition; no new language review.

changes.before: Taxanes are chemotherapy drugs originally from the yew tree that freeze the cell's internal scaffolding so it cannot divide, widely used but causing nerve damage in hands and feet.
changes.after: Taxanes change how microtubules grow and shorten. These structures help cells divide and do other jobs, so healthy tissue can be affected too.
changes.disposition: Corrected simplified English from the adopted source-backed definition; no new language review.

changes.before: Alkylating agents glue DNA strands together so cells cannot copy them, while antimetabolites are fake building blocks that jam DNA synthesis, the two oldest chemotherapy families.
changes.after: These are two different drug families. Alkylating agents attach chemical groups to molecules such as DNA; antimetabolites interfere with chemicals cells normally use.
changes.disposition: Corrected simplified English from the adopted source-backed definition; no new language review.

changes.before: Tubulin builds the microtubule scaffolding a cell needs to pull its chromosomes apart, and taxanes freeze it while vinca alkaloids and eribulin stop it forming, so dividing cells stall and die.
changes.after: Tubulin builds microtubules used in division, transport and cell organisation. Medicines can change these structures without every exposed cell dying.
changes.disposition: Corrected simplified English from the adopted source-backed definition; no new language review.
